title: Slime Mold Network Optimization Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a Three.js slime mold (Physarum polycephalum) network optimization simulation. The simulation models how slime mold finds efficient networks between food sources, inspired by real biological behavior.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 40, 50) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (0x334455, intensity 0.3) and a directional light (0xffeedd, intensity 0.8) from (10, 30, 10).
- Create a dark ground plane (60x60, color 0x0a0a12) at y=0 representing the petri dish surface.
- Load 'Lantern.glb' using GLTFLoader from CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.163.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Scale the lantern model to 0.8 and place 5 instances at fixed positions as 'food sources': (-18,0,-18), (18,0,-18), (0,0,20), (-20,0,10), (15,0,12). Each lantern emits a faint point light (0xffaa44, intensity 0.5, distance 8).
- OrbitControls for camera.

SLIME MOLD SIMULATION:
- Maintain an array of 300 'agent' particles representing slime mold explorers. Each agent has: position (x,z on the ground plane), heading (angle in radians), speed (0.05-0.15 units/frame).
- Use a 120x120 trail map (2D Float32Array) storing pheromone concentration values [0..1]. The trail map covers the 60x60 ground plane.
- Each simulation tick: (1) agents sense pheromone ahead-left, ahead, ahead-right at sensor distance 3.0 and sensor angle 0.4 rad, (2) agents turn toward highest pheromone, (3) agents move forward and deposit pheromone 0.05 at their position, (4) trail map diffuses (3x3 box blur) and decays by factor 0.97.
- Food sources (lantern positions) continuously emit pheromone (set trail map value to 1.0 in a radius of 3 cells around each food source each tick).
- Visualize agents as a THREE.Points object with small yellow-green dots (size 0.3, color 0x99ff33).
- Visualize the trail map as a PlaneGeometry with a DataTexture (120x120, single channel mapped to color: black=0, bright yellow-green=1). Update this texture every frame.

NETWORK EXTRACTION:
- Maintain a network graph: nodes (food sources) and edges (connections between them).
- Every 60 ticks, analyze the trail map: for each pair of food sources, sample pheromone values along the straight line between them. If the average pheromone along the path exceeds a threshold of 0.15, consider them 'connected'. Store edges as an array of {from, to, strength} objects.
- Visualize active edges as glowing line segments (THREE.Line with 0x44ff88 color) between connected food source positions at y=0.5.
- Compute total network length (sum of Euclidean distances of active edges) and track it.

SIMULATION CONTROLS:
- The simulation starts PAUSED. A DOM button 'Start' (id='startBtn') begins the simulation.
- A 'Pause/Resume' button (id='pauseBtn') toggles pause.
- A 'Reset' button (id='resetBtn') resets all agents to random positions, clears the trail map, clears edges, resets tick count to 0.
- A speed slider (id='speedSlider', range 1-5, default 1) controls how many simulation ticks run per animation frame.
- A 'Decay Rate' slider (id='decaySlider', range 0.90-0.99, step 0.01, default 0.97) adjusts pheromone decay.
- Keyboard 'A' adds 50 new agents at random positions. Keyboard 'R' is same as reset button. Keyboard 'Space' toggles pause.
- Clicking on the 3D canvas (raycasting to ground plane) places a new temporary food source at that position (max 3 temporary sources). Temporary food sources are shown as small spheres (radius 0.5, color 0xff4444). They are stored separately and also emit pheromone.

UNDO/REDO:
- Pressing 'Z' undoes the last temporary food source placement (removes it). Pressing 'Y' redoes it. Maintain an undo stack and redo stack for temporary food sources only.

HUD:
- A HUD overlay (id='hud') in top-left showing: Tick count, Agent count, Active edges count, Total network length (2 decimal places), Simulation state (PAUSED/RUNNING).

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
Expose and continuously update:
- simulationState: 'paused' | 'running'
- tickCount: number
- agentCount: number
- agents: array of {x, z, heading} (first 10 only for performance)
- foodSources: array of {x, z, isTemporary} for all food sources
- tempFoodCount: number
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- trailMapSum: sum of all trail map values (number)
- edges: array of {from, to, strength}
- edgeCount: number
- totalNetworkLength: number
- decayRate: number
- speedMultiplier: number
- lanternLoadedCount: number (how many Lantern.glb instances loaded successfully)
- pheromoneAtFood: average pheromone value in 3-cell radius around first fixed food source
- conservationCheck: agentCount === points geometry count (boolean)
physics_constraints: Pheromone values must remain in [0,1]. Trail map decay must be multiplicative (value *= decayRate each tick). Agents must stay within the 60x60 ground plane bounds (wrap around edges). Total pheromone deposited per tick = agentCount * 0.05 + foodSourceEmission. Network length must equal sum of Euclidean distances of active edges. Agent count must always match the Points geometry vertex count.
